question: For a Software Engineer III .NET role at Walmart, the second round was mostly conceptual: core C# and .NET Core concepts, the Observer and State design patterns, basic low-level design (LLD) questions and OOP fundamentals. The interviewer was checking clarity of fundamentals rather than depth.
lookingFor: Clear explanations of OOP pillars with concrete C# examples
Knowing when to apply Observer and State, and how they differ
Familiarity with .NET Core features (DI, middleware, async/await)
Ability to turn a short requirement into classes and interfaces
followUps: How do events and delegates work in C#, and how do you avoid event-related memory leaks?
Difference between abstract class and interface in C#?
Explain singleton, scoped and transient lifetimes with an example.
